steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

To make the crust: Pulse almonds in a food processor until finely ground, then pour into a medium bowl. Add graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and salt. Pour in melted butter and mix until evenly moistened. Press into a 9-inch pie plate.
Bake in the preheated oven until crust is golden brown, 10 to 13 minutes.

While crust is baking, make the filling: Beat condensed milk, cream, egg yolks, and lime zest in a large bowl until well combined. Whisk in lime juice, a little at a time, to thicken custard. Pour custard into pie crust.
Bake until custard is set, about 15 minutes. Cool to room temperature on a wire rack, then cover loosely with plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for 8 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Phoenician's Key Lime Pie
raw_recipe.description: This delicious Key lime pie recipe has a ground toasted almond crust with a creamy and refreshing filling flavored with Key lime juice and zest.

review.reviewBody: Phoenician Gourmet, you have outdone yourself and this pie absolutely deserves to be titled after you! I have my favorite Key Lime Pie recipe that I have been using for years, and I don't mind saying this recipe will probably take its place. First of all, the crust -the ground, toasted almonds take it to way beyond the ordinary. And then there's the filling - SO extra creamy! The heavy cream was a beautiful addition not only in taste, but its addition makes for a more substantial pie than others, filling the pie plate nicely. The combination of the novel ingredients of almonds and cream make for one, extraordinarily good Key Lime Pie, and with the perfect degree of lime flavor! As the first reviewer of this recipe, I can only strongly encourage others to give it a try! I can't imagine you'd be sorry! Edited 8/7/2011 - I use 1-1/2 tsp. grated lime zest rather than just 1/2 tsp. - perfect.

Fantastic recipe, when key limes are in season, stock up on them, just put in freezer and they are good for about a year, when needed, just take out what you need, better than the bottle stuff, i like my limes fresh, I have frozen lemon and limes and oranges for years. and just as good as the day I got them. 
From Peyton in Mississauga

I added 1T of regular lime zest. I like it very lime-ey. To the crust I also added 1/2 c of toasted coconut. Chopped all in the food processor fine and add enough melted butter to make “wet sand” mixture. I then used 4-6 oz ramekins. Packed 1/4 cup of crust mixture in each ramekin & baked for 10-15 min @ 350°. I then filled each ramekin with equal amounts of custard mixture and baked for an additional 15min @ 350°. Pulled them, let cool for a few min then covered and refrigerated. Garnished with whipped cream and lime zest or curls.

Amazing! I made a small change to it. Did pistachios instead of almonds and only did 1/4 cups gram crackers and the rest nuts. Amazing change and flavor that compliments the limes. Also used a spring pan instead of a pie plate.

This is just my first time to comment. 
This is always a flawless dessert! I have used this recipe for several years and made it countless times for cook outs and other gatherings. I usually make two at a time. I double the recipe but start with store-bought graham cracker crusts. I use the left over egg whites and brush the crusts and bake at 375 for 5-8 min. I know you're asking about the almond flavor, but hold on...
I use the zest from a whole lime. Be sure it is ripe/dark green all the way around. I then drop a cup (+/-) of sliced almonds in the mix since the flavor is not in the crust. This method allows for all the flavors of the original with an easier clean up.

This is a great recipe but I made a few changes because I love the taste of lime and possibly due to my having to use regular limes instead of key limes. I used 3/4 cup of lime juice, 3/4 teaspoon of grated lime zest and added 3-4 drops of concentrated lime oil for the filling. I then sprinkled another 3/4 teaspoon of grated lime zest on top of the filling, before baking, for decoration.

Once baked I prepared whipped cream - added 3/4 drops of the lime oil to the whipping cream and sugar.

The best key lime pie I have ever had. My husband loved this. I added an extra egg yolk and lime zest. Spray pie plate with Pam before adding graham cracker crust. I had a terrible time removing crust from pie plate.
Got rave reviews from all that ate it. I made it with almond flour and through all the crust ingredients in a food processor then patted it into a pie pan.
I purchase a pecan crust which saves a step. I add two drops of green food coloring. Easy to make for a special dessert.

I have been wanting to make this pie forever. Yesterday I got a chance to make it for my Memorial day dinner. I loved the idea of putting nuts in the crust. I decided to put my own spin on it by crushing Lorna Doone cookies and macadamia nuts. I also made the recipe 50% bigger, because I had an extra large pie pan. I baked the pie for 25 minutes instead of 15 to make up for the size difference. This pie was exceptional! I will be making it again.

I made a little variation and everybody loved it. I added a meringue on top.
To Make Meringue: In a large glass or metal mixing bowl, beat the remaining egg whites until foamy (that you can turn the bowl upside down and it doesn't fall). Gradually add sugar, continuing to beat until whites form stiff peaks. add few drops of ppepermint extract and keep beating. Spread meringue over pie covering completely.
hope you like it!!!!

It was overwhelmingly cloyingly sweet. Unfortunately, I baked it for neighbors and ultimately, I gave it a 52 out of 100. It was so bad. I’m embarrassed truth be told. It’s my fault. I used about 25 key limes hand squeezy one of them used Biscoff cookies as the crust which was good but the actual filling was horrid

First time I made it as directed. I loved the filling. I wasn't a fan of the almond crust. The second time, I made the pie filling, added a teaspoon more of lime zest and used a crust recipe using 1 cup graham cracker crumbs and 1 cup biscoff cookie crumbs. The filling with this crust was amazing.
Fantastic....I made this for a get together and it was the highlight of the evening! Definitely worth making again and again!

I made exactly as written. No substitute. On Christmas Day for my boyfriend a native of Florida whose favorite is key lime pie. Was a bit nervous but he among others that tried the pie said it was great! Will be making again.
Our granddaughter insists we make this ,because it's the best!

Used 1/2 cup sour cream instead of heavy cream. Used a different almond crust recipe - all almond flour, no graham crackers. Gluten free and gluten friendly guests all dazzled. Nellie & Joe's key lime juice.
This is my husband’s request for his birthday dessert every year. So easy and basically fool-proof. Oh, and did I mention delicious?
